FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Monday, May 4th, 2026 SENATOR RISCH MOVES FAST TO SILENCE ACHILLES’ CAMPAIGN BILLBOARD Risch protects his private land with an urgency he won't apply to stopping the lease of public lands to foreign interests. BOISE, Idaho — Idaho independent U.S. Senate candidate Todd Achilles confirmed today that a series of campaign billboards recently displayed across the Gem State has drawn an unexpected, but telling response from his opponent, three-term Senator, Jim Risch. Campaign staff received a call last week informing them that one of their rented billboard locations sits on land owned by Senator Risch, and that the Senator demanded it be taken down immediately. The Achilles campaign had no prior knowledge that the advertising agency it contracted with had leased space on Risch-owned property. Given that Senator Risch owns tens of millions of dollars' worth of land across Idaho, the campaign notes that avoiding his holdings entirely may be a practical impossibility. "It looks like Senator Risch proudly stands for free speech — as long as it's speech he agrees with," said Achilles. "He tells Idahoans he stands for public lands, while voting for nominees and legislation that sell them out. B ut when it comes to defending his own personal holdings, he wastes no time whatsoever. Given his 2023 attempt to abuse his position to reroute B oise air traffic away from his 44-acre ranch in Meridian, maybe we shouldn't be surprised." The issue of public lands — a defining concern for the Achilles campaign and one that resonates deeply with Idahoans across the political spectrum — came into sharp focus with Risch's reaction. "A pparently, unleashing a foreign mining company on Minnesota's B oundary Waters is a perfectly fine idea," Achilles said, "but one of our billboards sitting on one of his acres — that's where Jim draws the line. That's what he will fight for. It's genuinely nice to see him passionate about something. It's just a shame that something isn't the wellbeing of the people of Idaho." Achilles added: "For a politician who rarely speaks to his own constituents, this moment makes it very clear where he really stands on free speech — and whose land he is actually willing to protect." www.achillesforidaho.com

ABOUT TODD ACHILLES Todd Achilles, 58, is an Army veteran, former state legislator, public policy professor, and technology executive. He grew up on a family farm, served as a U.S. Army tank commander and armor officer, spent over 20 years in senior leadership roles at T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard, and several technology startups, and served in the Idaho House of Representatives before resigning in July 2025 to launch his U.S. Senate campaign. He lives in Boise with his family. For media inquiries 208-254-0002 info@achillesforidaho.com www.achillesforidaho.com
